clue.text: Reportedly how couple split cost of wig?

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are judged by how they are spoken, giving a word of matching sound

parts.note: a couple sharing a bill means two of them pay, said as two words

explanation.surface: A question about how a pair might share the price of a hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'two pay' (what a couple splitting a cost do) is the same as the word for a small hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpiece worn to cover a bald patch is a small wig.

clue.text: Sweet wine is fine with last of dessert

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the word dessert is taken

parts.note: fine and okay both mean acceptable

explanation.surface: A sweet wine judged fine to go with the end of a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes T, the final letter of 'dessert'; it goes in front of OKAY ('fine'), the charade being in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine.

clue.text: International body clothing? Lack of it, rather

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is an international body
dress is a general word for clothing

explanation.surface: A pondering on whether an international organisation is about clothes, or rather a lack of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's own 'clothing': 'lack of it' is a state of having none on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of undress means being naked or only partly clothed, a lack of garments.

clue.text: Ballerinas need this ability for promotion

definitions.meaning: in ballet the term names a dancer's ability to leap high
a promotion raises someone to a higher rank

explanation.definitionFit: In ballet the word names a dancer's height in jumps, and generally it means raising someone up in rank.

clue.text: Jack starts on the bottle

parts.note: a jack is a ship's flag, as in the Union Jack
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Jack starts drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is not a name but a flag flown on a ship; 'starts' is a link word saying the pieces begin the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider.

clue.text: Not very alcoholic-match the answer 'to a crossword clue

definitions.meaning: a beer low in alcohol is described as weak or low-strength
a match is something you strike for a flame, a means of ignition
in crossword jargon each grid entry is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Light beer is weak, a light is a flame-giver such as a match, and solvers call each grid entry a light.

clue.text: Strive to obtain objective and choose Italian

parts.note: to go for something is to choose it

explanation.surface: Advice to pursue a goal and pick the Italian option.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom urging someone to make a full attempt at a goal.

clue.text: Is introduced to the subtleties irritating people

indicators.note: introduced to means the first piece is put inside the second

parts.note: subtleties are fine shades of meaning, nuances
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is shown fine distinctions, which annoys people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' reads in the surface as meeting someone; here it is the insertion signal, with 'Is' going inside the word for subtleties.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests and annoying people are called nuisances.

clue.text: Son pretended to have slid out of control

parts.note: to kid is to pretend or tease

explanation.surface: A boy faked having lost control on a slippery surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that skids slides without the driver's control.

clue.text: Drink what's put in break fast cup and fly into rage

parts.words: what's put in break fast cup
parts.note: a breakfast egg cup holds a boiled egg
to flip is to lose one's temper

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over a breakfast cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break fast' is split to disguise breakfast, and the cup is an egg cup.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg flip is a drink of beaten egg mixed with beer or spirits.

clue.text: Nearly time to put on clobber for entertainment venue

parts.note: nigh means nearly
to clobber is to club, to hit hard

explanation.surface: It is almost time to get dressed in one's gear for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' is British slang for clothes, which the surface uses, but here it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a late-opening venue for dancing and drinks.

clue.text: Why mistake eccentric for chap from Winchester?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question of why an odd error is made about a Winchester man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the letters of WHY MISTAKE. Winchester College is an old English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils and old boys of Winchester College are named after its founder William of Wykeham.

clue.text: Bring up the tail

definitions.meaning: to bring up children is to raise them
the tail is the back end of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to raise young as a verb, and the hindmost part as a noun; 'bring up the rear' also means to come last.

clue.text: They hit the low notes when appearing in British Standards Institution

indicators.note: appearing in means one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: the British Standards Institution is abbreviated BSI
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Singers who reach low notes turn up at the British standards body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' reads as performing at a venue, but signals insertion; 'when' is the link-like word supplying letters. Bassi is the Italian plural of basso.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass singers sing the lowest part; the Italian plural is used for them.

clue.text: One dispenses alcohol with skill during drinking bout

indicators.note: during means the skill sits within the drinking bout

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art means skill

explanation.surface: Someone who skilfully serves drinks in the middle of a heavy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals insertion: the skill goes inside a slang word for a drinking session, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mixes and serves drinks at a bar dispenses alcohol.

clue.text: Rick has tacky version

indicators.note: a version is a different form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Rick owns a cheap and tasteless edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges HAS TACKY. 'Rick' looks like a name but is a farming word for a stack.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a large stack of hay or straw.

clue.text: Not a short measure of beer for a lady drunk with ecstasy

definitions.text: Not a short measure of beer

indicators.note: drunk means the words are muddled into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A large beer for a woman who is drunk and on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges FOR A LADY, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a tall glass about a yard long, holding a large quantity of beer.

clue.text: Brandy anagram complicated by first letter of clue

indicators.note: complicated means the letters are tangled into a new order
first letter of means just the opening letter of the word clue

explanation.surface: A setter describes making a brandy anagram harder by adding a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges ANAGRAM, then 'first letter of' adds C from 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony in France.

clue.text: A front-row forward, very big, would be appropriate

parts.note: in rugby a prop is a front-row forward
OS is short for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A huge rugby forward would suit the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby's props play in the front row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means fitting or relevant to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Group of drivers add point to point to Ascot events perhaps

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation
E, east, is a compass point
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Motorists join point-to-point racing at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point to point' looks like a horse race but gives two compass points. Ascot is an English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse, so its events are horse races.

clue.text: Convention in Spain offers a sedative

parts.note: a code is a set of conventions
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An agreement in Spain provides a calming drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate used to relieve pain and calm.

clue.text: Drink is better when nondrinker has gone

indicators.note: has gone means the nondrinker is taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
TT, teetotal, describes someone who never drinks alcohol

explanation.surface: A drink is better once a teetotaller has left.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic drink brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: Time soldier is in one place to amend four customs

definitions.text: Time soldier is in one place

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: customs are duties charged on imports

explanation.surface: Changing four customs procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amend' rearranges only 'four' to UROF; the surface makes it act on 'four customs'. The definition describes a posting served at one station.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of duty is a period of service posted at one station.

clue.text: Cloth for very pretty daughter

parts.note: twee means excessively pretty

explanation.surface: Fabric for a daughter who is very sweet-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen fabric.

clue.text: Ceasefire note covers Ulster police

indicators.note: covers means the note goes round the police, holding them inside

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A truce is announced as a message reaches the Northern Irish police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' signals that the musical note wraps round the police initials. The RUC was renamed in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting.

clue.text: Notice more suitable and versatile electrical connector

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
apter is more apt

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a better and more flexible plug.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter lets a plug fit a socket of a different type.

clue.text: Fish for Henry -one only

parts.note: Hal is a short form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
I is the Roman numeral for one
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A fish just for one Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Halibut is a large flatfish.

clue.text: Hang out with front two in reserve team

indicators.note: front two in means the first two letters of the word reserve are taken

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: Spending time with the leading pair of the second string.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang out in a place, informally, is to live there.

clue.text: A clergyman, before worship

parts.note: Rev, reverend, is a title for a clergyman
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A vicar arriving ahead of the service.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to honour deeply, close to worship.
